slot.brief: decide intervals where a simple polynomial/rational function is increasing or decreasing by testing the sign of f′(x)

stem: The interval in which f(x) = x^3 - 3x + 4 is decreasing is
working:
f'(x) = 3x^2 - 3 = 3(x - 1)(x + 1). f'(x) < 0 when (x - 1)(x + 1) < 0, i.e. -1 < x < 1. Hence f is decreasing on (-1, 1).

Independent check: f'(x)=3x^2-3=3(x-1)(x+1), which is negative for -1<x<1.
solution:
A function is decreasing where $f'(x)<0$. Here,
$$f'(x)=3x^2-3=3(x-1)(x+1)<0$$
for $-1<x<1$. Hence, $f$ is decreasing on $(-1,1)$.
